incident: Ryuk's Return (BazarLoader/Kegtap to domain-wide Ryuk in 29 hours)

sources.title: Ryuk's Return - The DFIR Report (2020-10-08)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (malspam -> Bazar/Kegtap Document-Preview.exe), hops (beachhead->DC via SMB/WMIC + service, DC pivot->backup over SMB, SMB/RDP to others), Kerberoast (Rubeus), exfil (vsftpd of AdFind/Rubeus output to Russia), impact (Ryuk backups first then domain), 29h

narrative_before: In a 2020 intrusion the DFIR Report observed malspam delivering a Bazar/Kegtap loader: a user ran 'Document-Preview.exe' which beaconed to 5.182.210[.]145 over 443 and injected into explorer.exe/svchost.exe on the beachhead host. On day 1 the actors checked a domain controller for MS17-010 (not vulnerable) and dropped a Cobalt Strike beacon on a DC, which became their 'main operations point' (C2 to martahzz[.]com). First lateral movement came about 28 hours after entry, with the backup server reached over SMB roughly an hour later. On day 2 Kerberoasting was attempted with Rubeus and AdFind/Rubeus output was exfiltrated over vsftpd to 45.141.84[.]120 (Russia). Ryuk was staged and run from the pivot DC, hitting backup servers first (Veeam/SQL stopped, wbadmin used) then the rest of the domain; the report states the campaign ran 29 hours from initial execution to domain-wide ransomware with a 600+ BTC (~$6M) demand.

machines.name: dc
machines.role: domain controller (Cobalt Strike beacon, main operations point / Ryuk staging)

machines.name: srv_backup
machines.role: backup server (reached over SMB; Veeam/SQL stopped, wbadmin; encrypted first)

detection_moments.description: Beachhead Bazar/Kegtap loader executing and beaconing; initial discovery (net, nltest). Earliest observable moment.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the user ran Document-Preview.exe which connected to 5.182.210[.]145 over 443' - Ryuk's Return, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: ~28h after entry: Cobalt Strike beacon dropped on a domain controller via SMB+WMIC/service; DC is the actor's main operations point before ransomware staging.
detection_moments.evidence: 'a Cobalt Strike beacon was dropped via SMB, then WMIC was used to run it ... the DC became the threat actors main operations point' - Ryuk's Return

detection_moments.description: Day 2: Kerberoasting with Rubeus; backup server reached over SMB from the DC pivot ~1h after first lateral; discovery output exfiltrated via vsftpd.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Kerberoasting was attempted on Day 2 using Rubeus ... DC pivot -> backup server: SMB, roughly one hour after the first lateral movement' - Ryuk's Return

attack_path: malspam Bazar/Kegtap loader run by user (T1566/T1204)
Cobalt Strike beacon copied over SMB and executed via WMIC / remote service (T1021.002/T1047)
SMB lateral movement from DC pivot to backup server ~1h after first hop (T1021.002)
Ryuk copied over SMB and executed via RDP from the pivot DC (T1021.002/T1021.001/T1486)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; the report uses placeholder hostnames.
No defender detection timeline given; moments are the report's own activity markers (first execution, DC pivot, day-2 Kerberoast/backup).
Domain admin acquisition not explicitly described; Kerberoast attempted. Counts of encrypted servers/workstations not given (modelled as srv_1, pc_2).
